title: A drag re-renders the strip on every pointermove, even inside one day
body:
## Summary
TimeStrip's move handler calls setDrag with a fresh object on every pointermove, so a drag re-renders the whole strip (bars() over every day, ticks()) at pointer rate even while the pointer stays in one slot.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/TimeStrip.tsx:64 `if (drag !== null) setDrag({ a: drag.a, b: i })` - a new object each event defeats React's same-state bail-out; hover (line 65) bails because it is a primitive. Fixed: set only when `drag.b !== i`. On the Ledger the strip is 98 days; each render recomputes 98 bars and the tick walk.

## Flow
- pointerdown on the strip, move 40 px inside one day slot -> ~N pointermove events -> N TimeStrip renders
- fix: guard the setter on a changed slot; same for setHover is already free

## Expected impact
A drag stays at one render per slot crossed instead of one per event. Could break nothing visible; the brush only moves on a slot change anyway.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - renders per drag proportional to slots crossed, not pointer events
Before: predicted: one render per pointermove (code read: new object per event)
After: predicted: one render per slot change
Method: simulation - the package lane has no DOM (no jsdom/happy-dom installed) and the live lane is not this agent's to run; a React Profiler count needs one
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: tests/live ledger spec: a React Profiler onRender counter (or a data-render attribute) around TimeStrip; drag 40 px inside one slot, count renders (expect N -> 1); seed red by removing the guard

title: Every hovered day is announced: the hover readout lives in the live region
body:
## Summary
The strip's readout div is aria-live=polite and holds the hovered day's counts, so sweeping the pointer across the strip queues one announcement per day crossed.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/TimeStrip.tsx:83-97: the live region exists so a keyboard user hears the range set through the URL (header lines 7-10), but the hover branch renders inside the same region. A screen-reader user with a pointer (magnifier users, touch exploration) hears a queue of `14 Oct · 37 ev ...`. Fixed: the region holds only the resting sentence; the hover readout is drawn beside it aria-hidden (its numbers are the bars' own, already in the grid).

## Flow
- hover across 10 days with a screen reader on -> 10 polite announcements
- fix: split the readout into a live resting line and an aria-hidden hover line

## Expected impact
Assistive-tech users hear the range, not the pointer's path. Could break: a pointer-driven SR user loses the per-day counts unless the bars get names.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - announcements per hover sweep 10 -> 0, range announcement kept
Before: predicted 1 announcement per day crossed (code read)
After: predicted 0 for hover, 1 per range change
Method: simulation - announcements need a browser with a live-region observer; no DOM in the package lane
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: live spec: MutationObserver on [aria-live] inside [data-component=TimeStrip], hover across 10 day slots, count text mutations (10 -> 0), then drag a range and require exactly 1

title: The Ledger toolbar rounds its cost before usd() for the chip but not its name
body:
## Summary
Toolbar.tsx calls usd(Number(cost.total.toFixed(2))) for the visible chip and usd(cost.total) for its accessible name: two roundings of one figure.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Toolbar.tsx:107. The pre-round was a workaround for usd() choosing decimals from the unrounded figure; acad6377 made usd() round to the cent first, so the workaround is now a second rounding rule (toFixed's binary-exact rounding vs Math.round(x*100)) that can still disagree at a half cent. Fixed: one call, usd(cost.total), for both.

## Flow
- grep -n 'toFixed(2)' Toolbar.tsx -> 1 site
- fix: drop the Number(...toFixed(2)) wrapper

## Expected impact
Visible and spoken totals always match. Could break nothing: usd() already rounds.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rounding rule for the toolbar's cost
Before: 2 roundings of one figure (Toolbar.tsx:107)
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - the site is in ledger-screen's paths, not this round's
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server toolbar render: total 9.995 / 0.004 -> the chip's value equals the name's figure; seed red with the wrapper restored and a total where toFixed and Math.round disagree

title: Crumbs keys its steps by label, so two steps with one name collide
body:
## Summary
Crumbs.tsx keys each trail step by c.label; a trail where two levels share a name (a part named like its project) gives React two siblings with one key.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/crumbs/Crumbs.tsx:12 `<Fragment key={c.label}>`. Trails are built by callers from data (PartWorkspace's p.trail, Library Toolbar's kind label), so a duplicate is reachable. React then warns and may reuse the wrong step's DOM on a trail change. Fixed: key by position (a trail is ordered and short) or by href/label+index.

## Flow
- render Crumbs trail=[{label:'Intro',href:'/p/1'},{label:'Intro',href:'/p/1/a'}] -> React duplicate-key error on the client

## Expected impact
Breadcrumbs stay correct when names repeat. Could break nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a trail with repeated names renders without key collision
Before: predicted: duplicate-key warning (code read)
After: predicted: none
Method: simulation - react-dom/server does not report duplicate keys; the reconciler (a DOM) does, and the package lane has none
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: a live spec (or a jsdom vitest once a DOM lib exists) rendering a two-step same-label trail with console.error captured: 1 duplicate-key error -> 0

title: The strip's due marks were promised with the publish source, which landed without them
body:
## Summary
strip.ts says the prototype's `due` marks (scheduled publish slots) 'arrive with the publish source'; the publish source exists and reads schedule.json, and the strip still draws no due mark.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/strip.ts:14-16 (header). lib/ledger/v1/sources/publish.ts reads <publish store>/schedule.json and lists slots (listSlots). Neither DayCount nor Bar carries a due flag, and app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts hands the strip none. The same paragraph's reason for dropping the `session` segment ('nothing writes from the studio in Phase 2') is also stale: the studio's own acts are written to the ledger (lib/decision/v1/sources/*.ts) and drawn as `operator`. Fixed: either draw due days (a `due` count on DayCount from the slot read, a mark per day) or restate the header as a decision.

## Flow
- read strip.ts:14-16 -> promise
- grep listSlots lib/ledger/v1/sources/publish.ts -> the source has landed
- grep due packages/ui/src/components/timestrip -> 0 marks

## Expected impact
The Ledger strip shows what is scheduled ahead of NOW (the hatched future days are otherwise always empty), or the header stops promising it. Could break: the strip's DayCount type gains a field every caller fills.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - 2 stale claims in strip.ts's header -> 0, and the due marks drawn
Before: 2 claims the tree contradicts
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - drawing them needs read.ts (ledger-screen) to supply due days
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: ledger.test.ts: bars() over a DayCount with due:2 yields a due mark on that day (0 -> 1); tests/next-server ledger-read: a fixture schedule slot on a future day reaches strip.days[i].due

title: The strip's range has no keyboard path on the strip itself
body:
## Summary
TimeStrip sets a range only from pointer events; a keyboard user reaches a range only by editing the URL or the toolbar's date chips.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/TimeStrip.tsx:101-112: the bars group has onPointerDown/Move/Up and no tabIndex or key handler; the header (lines 7-10) names the URL as the keyboard path. Registry table technique `grid-keyboard-model` and `one-door-for-range-writes`: a range control reachable by pointer only. Fixed: the bars group is focusable, Left/Right move a day cursor that drives the same readout, Shift+arrows extend, Enter applies through the same onRange door, Esc clears.

## Flow
- Tab to the strip -> no stop
- build: a cursor state, key handler calling dragRange(keys, a, b, range) - the same pure function a drag uses

## Expected impact
Keyboard and SR users can pick a day range where the data is drawn. Could break: the Ledger's own key map (a strip key must not shadow a list key).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard range selection 0 of 4 cases -> 4 of 4 (focus, move, extend, apply)
Before: 0 of 4
After: predicted 4 of 4
Method: simulation - needs a live spec; the package lane has no DOM
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/live ledger spec: focus the strip, ArrowRight x3, Shift+ArrowRight x2, Enter -> URL from/to equal the 4th..6th day; seed red with the key handler removed

title: The cost column mixes two-decimal and whole-dollar figures
body:
## Summary
usd() draws cents under $10 and whole dollars above, so one right-aligned cost column holds `$0.42` and `$47`; the decimal points do not align.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/eventrow/usd.ts (rule kept from the prototype's fmtUsd), drawn in EventRow's `.c` column (EventRow.module.css:30, tabular-nums, right-aligned). Registry table golden path: 'units and precision decided per column, once - not per cell' and 'numbers right-aligned, in tabular numerals, so magnitudes align'. The prototype chose the mixed rule deliberately (a cent visible where it matters); changing it changes every money figure in the studio.

## Flow
- Ledger list: a $0.42 row above a $47 row -> the units digits do not line up

## Expected impact
A cost column the eye can scan by magnitude. Could break: every pinned money spelling across the studio.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one precision per money column
Before: 2 precisions in one column
After: 1
Method: simulation - a taste call against the prototype's own rule
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
